title: Learning and Steering in Incomplete-Information Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.07589v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In many modern multi-agent systems, a mediator seeks to influence strategic decision dynamics using only outcome-level feedback and without knowing agents' utilities. In this work, we study how a mediator can learn an unknown game and steer adaptive agents toward outcomes that maximize her utility using only trajectory feedback. The mediator knows the game form and her own objective, but not the agents' utilities. Moreover, she commits to nonnegative payments and provides recommendations and contexts, but receives only a single realized terminal outcome rather than full-information feedback. We develop halving-type algorithms that learn utility differences in normal-form games and conditional continuation-value differences in extensive-form games, achieving a sample complexity of $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ that matches worst-case lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. translated_title: 不完全信息博弈中的学习与引导
translated_abstract: 在许多现代多智能体系统中，调解者希望仅通过结果层面的反馈来影响策略性决策动态，而无需了解智能体的效用。在本工作中，我们研究调解者如何学习一个未知的博弈，并仅使用轨迹反馈将自适应的智能体引导至使其自身效用最大化的结果。调解者知道博弈的形式和自己的目标，但不知道智能体的效用。此外，她承诺支付非负的款项，并提供推荐和上下文信息，但她只能获得单个已实现的终端结果，而非全信息反馈。我们开发了二分类型（halving-type）算法，用于学习标准式博弈中的效用差异和扩展式博弈中的条件延续价值差异，实现了 $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ 的样本复杂度，在最坏情况下与下界仅相差对数因子。随后，我们将这些学习程序与拉格朗日方法相结合……
tldr: 该论文提出了仅利用轨迹反馈就能在不知道智能体效用的情况下学习标准式和扩展式博弈的二分类型算法，使调解者能够引导自适应智能体走向效用最大化的结果，并达到了近乎最优的样本复杂度。
